beats.subline: Thursday, September 3, 2026 close — stocks posted their best day since Aug. 4 as bond yields eased on dovish Fed signals.
beats.body: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller signaled openness to holding rates steady if inflation keeps improving, easing the 10-year Treasury yield and tempering the geopolitical jitters from the Iran conflict that had weighed on sentiment earlier in the week.

beats.headline: Iran accuses US of war crime over wedding strike; Vance calls the claim 'extremely skeptical'
beats.body: Iran says a Tuesday US strike hit a wedding celebration in Hormozgan province, killing four people and wounding dozens, and is seeking an ICC war-crimes investigation; at a Sept. 3 White House briefing, Vice President JD Vance dismissed the account, saying Iranian state media 'has not been a very good scribe about what's happened in the conflict,' while the Pentagon says it is reviewing the claim and maintains civilians are never intentionally targeted.

beats.headline: Taiwan defense report says PLA is prioritizing joint island-landing capability
beats.body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense told the Legislative Yuan its new 2026 China Military Power Report places new emphasis on the PLA's push to field joint island-landing capability, citing Type 076 amphibious assault ships, self-elevating landing barges, upgraded Z-20 helicopters and unmanned transport helicopters; analysts estimate the buildup could mature between 2030 and 2035, and the report says the PLA still cannot yet execute a full-scale landing campaign.

beats.headline: Iran hits US-linked bases in Kuwait and UAE for a second straight night
beats.body: Iran's military said it struck Ahmad al-Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Al Minhad Air Base in the UAE before dawn Thursday with drones and missiles, targeting satellite-communications gear, equipment warehouses, fighter hangars, troop positions and radar sites in retaliation for US strikes; Kuwait's Defense Ministry said its air defenses intercepted the attack and called it 'blatant Iranian aggression,' with no US casualties reported.

beats.headline: Army moves Palantir-Anduril TITAN targeting system from prototype to production
beats.body: The Army awarded a combined $192 million contract — $127 million to Palantir as prime, $65 million to Anduril — to produce eight Tactical Intelligence Targeting Access Node ground stations that fuse sensor data from joint and space-based assets to speed target detection and 'drastically reduce sensor-to-shooter timelines'; four corps-level advanced and four division-level basic variants are due for delivery over the next 18 months.

beats.headline: Claude suffers a roughly three-hour worldwide outage
beats.body: A wave of 529 'Overloaded' errors knocked out claude.ai, the API, Claude Code and Claude Cowork starting around 9:26 a.m. ET Wednesday, affecting Mythos 5.1, Fable 5.1 and Opus 5/4.8/4.6; Anthropic says the issue was resolved by 12:27 p.m. ET, a reminder of the operational risk of leaning on cloud AI for daily workflows.

beats.headline: Odunze and Swift leave Thursday's practice with injuries, both only questionable
beats.body: Wide receiver Rome Odunze left practice early after hobbling with a right-leg injury and running back D'Andre Swift came off holding his midsection, but both were listed only questionable for the Sept. 13 opener at Carolina, and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Swift's issue was just a cramp.

beats.headline: Byron says he's not a Chase favorite, will lean on tire management and track position at Darlington
beats.body: At Chevrolet's Sept. 2 Chase Media Day, the 13th-seeded Byron said 'we are not the favorites, and we know that,' calling that freeing heading into Sunday's Chase opener, and pointed to tire management, strong qualifying and staying up front as the keys at Darlington since 'the winners have come from the top-three the last few years.'

beats.headline: PCA presbyteries set September dates for a churchwide fast and prayer for revival
beats.body: Following the 53rd General Assembly's overture, presbyteries are appointing a day this month for congregations, RUF campus ministries, officers and members to fast and pray for 'the revival and renewal of the church,' with prayers for repentance, gospel advancement and church planting; Assembly moderator RE Mel Duncan has invited NAPARC sister churches and other evangelicals to join in.
